**Paris Get‑away: 7‑Day Itinerary (Spring/Summer)** *(Adjust dates and activities to fit your schedule and interests.)* | Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening | |-----|---------|-----------|---------| | **1 – Arrival & Orientation** | • Arrive at Charles de Gaulle or Orly.
• Take the RER B or a taxi to your hotel in the 7th, 8th, or 15th arrondissement (central, near major sights).
• Check‑in, freshen up. | • Walk along the Seine to Notre‑Dame & Île Saint‑Louis.
• Visit the **Musée d’Orsay** (if you’re into Impressionism). | • Dinner at a classic bistro in the Latin Quarter (e.g., **Le Coupe Chou**).
• Optional evening cruise on the Seine (Bateaux Mouches) to see illuminated landmarks. | | **2 – Classic Landmarks** | • Early breakfast at a local café.
• Visit the **Eiffel Tower** (book tickets online to skip the line). | • Picnic in Champ‑de‑Mars or a stroll through the Trocadéro Gardens.
• Explore the **Champs‑Élysées** and **Arc de Triomphe** (climb to the top for sunset). | • Dinner at **L’Atelier de Joël Robuchon** (Michelin‑starred, but affordable if you choose a prix‑fix menu).
• Night walk along the Seine to see the Eiffel Tower sparkle. | | **3 – Art & Culture** | • Breakfast at **Café Marly** overlooking the Louvre.
• Tour the **Louvre Museum** (focus on the Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, and Egyptian Antiquities). | • Lunch at **Le Café Marly** or a nearby sandwich shop.
• Visit the **Musée de l’Orangerie** (Monet’s Water Lilies). | • Dinner in the Marais (try **L’As du Fallafel** for a casual bite or **Café Charlot** for a classic vibe).
• Optional: Attend a jazz club in the Marais (e.g., **Le Caveau de la Huchette**). | | **4 – Day Trip to Versailles** | • Early train to Versailles (RER C).
• Tour the **Palace of Versailles** (Grand Apartments, Hall of Mirrors). | • Lunch at **La Petite Venise** inside the palace gardens.
• Explore the expansive **Gardens of Versailles** (tulips, fountains). | • Return to Paris.
• Light dinner near your hotel; perhaps try a crepe from a street vendor. | | **5 – Montmartre & Sacré‑Coeur** | • Breakfast at **Le Pain Quotidien**.
• Climb to **Sacré‑Coeur**; enjoy panoramic city views. | • Wander the cobblestone streets of Montmartre: Place du Tertre, Musée de Montmartre, and the **Espace Dalí**.
• Lunch at **Le Consulat** (historic café). | • Dinner at **La Maison Rose** (iconic Montmartre spot).
• Optional: Catch a cabaret show at **Moulin Rouge** or a smaller venue like **Le Lapin Agile**. | | **6 – Modern & Shopping** | • Breakfast at **Café Kitsuné** (famous for its Instagram‑ready aesthetic).
• Visit the **Centre Pompidou** (modern art, rooftop view). | • Lunch at **Le Georges** (restaurant on the Pompidou roof).
• Shop along Rue Saint‑Honoré, Le Bon Marché, or the boutiques of the 9th arrondissement. | • Dinner at **Septime** (Michelin‑starred, but book early for a tasting menu).
• Nightcap at a rooftop bar like **Le Perchoir**. | | **7 – Departure / Last‑Minute Exploration** | • Pack, check‑out, leave luggage at the hotel.
• Quick visit to the **Luxembourg Gardens** or the **Pantheon**. | • Grab a farewell lunch at **Le Relais de l’Entrecôte** (famous steak‑and‑french fries). | • Head to the airport; consider a last stroll along the Seine if time allows. | --- ### Practical Tips | Topic | Recommendation | |-------|----------------| | **Transportation** | • Buy a **Paris Visite** pass (valid for 2–5 days) covering metro, buses, RER, and trams.
• For day trips (Versailles, Giverny), use the RER or regional trains. | | **Accommodation** | • Central hotels: Hotel Le Meurice (luxury), Hôtel de la Porte Dorée (budget), or Airbnb in the 7th/8th arr.
• Book early for best rates. | | **Dining** | • Reserve restaurants 2–3 weeks ahead, especially Michelin‑starred spots.
• Try local specialties: croissants, escargot, coq au vin, macarons. | | **Tickets** | • Book major attractions (Eiffel Tower, Louvre, Versailles) online to avoid queues.
• Consider a **Paris Pass** for free entry to many museums and skip‑the‑line benefits. | | **Language** | • Basic French phrases help: “Bonjour”, “Merci”, “Où est…?”.
• Many locals speak English, especially in tourist areas. | | **Weather** | • Spring (April–June): 12–20 °C, occasional showers.
• Summer (July–August): 20–30 °C, hot afternoons.
• Pack layers, comfortable shoes, umbrella. | | **Safety** | • Keep an eye on your belongings in crowded places.
• Use official taxis or rideshare apps (Uber, Bolt). | | **Cash vs Card** | • Most places accept cards; keep some euros for small cafés or markets. | --- ### Optional Add‑Ons | Activity | Why It’s Worth It | |----------|-------------------| | **Giverny Day Trip** | Visit Monet’s house & gardens; perfect for art lovers. | | **Wine Tasting in Champagne** | Short train ride to Reims or Épernay; sample world‑famous sparkling wines. | | **Cooking Class** | Learn to make croissants or coq au vin with a local chef. | | **Night Market** | Explore the **Marché des Enfants Rouges** for street food. | | **Picnic at Parc des Buttes‑Chaumont** | Relax in a less‑touristy park with great city views. | Enjoy your Paris adventure! If you’d like more details on any specific day, dining reservations, or transportation options, just let me know.
